facts.fact_text: The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 12 January 2013 in Baku.
The opposition planned to hold a demonstration on 26 January 2013 in Baku.
Information about the demonstrations was disseminated through Facebook or the press.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
According to the applicant, the participants in the demonstration of 12 January 2013 were drawing the public's attention to the deaths of soldiers in the army.
According to the applicant, the participants in the demonstration of 26 January 2013 were condemning the use of force by the police against those who had participated in previous demonstrations.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 12 January 2013.
The applicant attended the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
At the time of both of the applicant's arrests, under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.
Shortly after the demonstration of 12 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
Shortly after the demonstration of 26 January 2013 had begun, the police started to disperse the assembly.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 12 January 2013.
The applicant was arrested during the dispersal operation of the demonstration of 26 January 2013.
On the day of the applicant's arrest on 12 January 2013, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued in respect of the applicant.
On the day of the applicant's arrest on 26 January 2013, an administrative-offence report (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) was issued in respect of the applicant.

The administrative-offence report issued on 12 January 2013 stated that the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law).

The administrative-offence report issued on 26 January 2013 stated that the applicant had committed an administrative offence under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (participation in a public assembly that had not been organised in accordance with the law).
In the first case (arrest of 12 January 2013), the applicant was brought before the Nasimi District Court on 14 January 2013, the day he reappeared at the police station.
In the second case (arrest of 26 January 2013), the applicant was brought before the Nasimi District Court on 26 January 2013, the day of his arrest.
By decision of 14 January 2013, the Nasimi District Court convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences in the first case.
By decision of 26 January 2013, the Nasimi District Court convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences in the second case.
In the first case, the Nasimi District Court sentenced the applicant to a fine of 500 Azerbaijani manats (AZN).
In the second case, the Nasimi District Court sentenced the applicant to a fine of AZN 400.
In the first case, on 25 January 2013, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal and upheld the decision of the Nasimi District Court.
In the second case, on 6 February 2013, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal and upheld the decision of the Nasimi District Court.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe expressed concern about recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code of Azerbaijan, which increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, 'unauthorised' gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code are likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the Commissioner is deeply concerned by the recent amendments to the Law on Freedom of Assembly, the Criminal Code and the Code of Administrative Offences of Azerbaijan, which further erode the right to freedom of assembly.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the sanctions which can now be imposed, coupled with the fact that local authorities have not authorised a single rally in Baku city centre in recent years, clearly have a chilling effect on the organisation of or participation in demonstrations.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the Commissioner is of the view that participants in peaceful assemblies should not be sanctioned for the mere fact of being present at and actively participating in the demonstration in question, provided they do not do anything illegal, violent or obscene in the course of it.

Report CommDH(2013)14 stated that the Commissioner urges the Azerbaijani authorities to ensure that no disproportionate sanction, which would undermine the fundamental right to peaceful assembly, is imposed.
